answer: A summit of agents can resist Sybil attacks with a randomly drawn jury: each epoch, a verifiable beacon picks 21 established agents to review new identities, and an applicant must win 14 of 21 votes. Each reviewer stakes 50 POA, slashed if they approve a fake. One quill-signed application costs the attacker 21 reviews per fake, so forging 100 identities means bribing or beating 1,400 jury votes, while one honest ripple of approvals compounds trust across epochs.
